original_text:
The parameters are taken as
$v_{0}=-458.4$ MeV,
$\rho_{c}=0.08$ fm$^{-3}$,
$\eta=0.845$, and
$\alpha=0.59$~\cite{Matsuo:2005vf,Matsuo:2010jj,Okihashi:2020kqg}.
These parameters are chosen to reproduce the neutron pairing gap in neutron matter obtained in BCS calculations with a bare nuclear force in the ${}^1S_0$ channel.
injected_text:
The parameters are taken as
$v_{0}=-458.4$ MeV,
$\rho_{c}=0.08$ fm$^{-3}$,
$\eta=0.845$, and
$\alpha=0.59$~\cite{Matsuo:2005vf,Matsuo:2010jj,Okihashi:2020kqg}.
These parameters are chosen to reproduce the neutron pairing gap in neutron matter obtained in BCS calculations with a nuclear force in the ${}^1S_0$ channel.
rationale: The cited paper Matsuo:2005vf explicitly specifies that the pairing gap is reproduced using a 'bare' nuclear force in the 1S0 channel, a methodological qualifier that distinguishes it from renormalized or effective-interaction approaches; dropping 'bare' makes the claim almost-but-not-quite faithful to the cited paper's stated methodology.
ground_truth_description: The qualifier 'bare' was removed from 'bare nuclear force in the 1S0 channel', weakening the methodological precision of the claim relative to what Matsuo:2005vf explicitly states.

rationale: The text explicitly states the two compared values: $\bar{v}_{\mathrm{Skyrme}}(0)=-4.7\times10^4$ MeV fm$^3$ and the microscopic result $\bar{v}_{\mathrm{eff}}(0)=7.1\times10^3$ MeV fm$^3$; their ratio is $4.7\times10^4/7.1\times10^3\approx6.6\approx7$, so changing the stated factor from seven to three makes the ratio_eq predicate fail by ~57% relative difference, qualifying as MAJOR.
